item.title: Another flipping flytip on the same spot, 15th September
item.description:
Oh what a surprise - not. On Sat 12th Sept I spotted a couple of small cardboard boxes on the pavement next to the utility cabinet at the side if Brewers. Between then and Mon 14th Sept they had been joined by other larger boxes, but the flytipper was "considerate" enough to put the smaller boxes inside them. We need CCTV at this spot immediately! I've made countless reports of flytipping on this same spot, yet you do nothing apart from send a clean up team each time. We need proper deterrents here, and CCTV will help you identify the culprits and prosecute them. There is no excuse for your lack of action.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 1, Clifton Road, Welling, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Safety hazard from incomplete zebra crossing at Worsley Bridge Road and Station Approach, 15th September
item.description:
I am incredibly frustrated that months ago contractors left the western side of the newly installed Zebra crossing’s zig-zag safety lines partially unpainted this summer simply because cars were in the way, despite easily finishing the middle and other side. Worse still, I can see online that other residents have repeatedly reported this blatant hazard, yet the Council keeps closing the tickets without doing any actual work. Vehicles are now regularly parking far too close to the crossing on the western side because of this missing paint, creating a highly dangerous blind spot for southbound traffic and pedestrians. Please escalate this to Highways immediately to get the job properly finished before someone gets hurt.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Worsley Bridge Road, New Beckenham, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Flytipping mix of domestic things and amazon style packaging blocking the fire exit from 2a highshore road, 14th September
item.description:
Please can you help : once again wierd domestic fly tipping has been dumped against the fire exit door and spilling onto the pavement. This is a regular occurrence. Please could you contact our managing agents Brunsfield to remind them of their statutory duty to ensure that fire exits are kept clear and in good order. Brunsfield ignore our reminders and requests for help.. and have done so since 2018! the other photos show the second fire exit.. a cesspit of urine and human waste, vomit, and so on. it builds up over time to prevent the exit from opening. This is also a health risk. the door is used by staff and deliveries by staff and deliveries to the fast food restaurant and the express supermarket that share the building with us, and by residents to access communal refuse and recycling and meter. the mess gets into the tread of our shoes and we bring it into the building and into our own flats ! not very pleasant. thank you.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 32, Rye Lane, Peckham, Greater London

item.title: Maiden Lane, Crayford needs care!, 14th September
item.description:
After walking my daughter to her new school, we have to cut through maiden lane, the alley way at the very end is vile, we have to play a game where we hold our breath and run… it’s not fair. It’s full of rubbish, a broken fence and animal poop. That’s just the start, we then walk up to the school and the whole of maiden lane’s pathways are full of poop, smashed glass, rubbish. The roads are just terrible and falling apart. It honestly is so neglected. It’s very upsetting seeing school children of young age dodging all these unnecessary obstacles! And young children are very clumsy and I really hope they don’t accidentally have a fall! Please can something be done to clean up the streets, there is also a bush near the school on the corner by the crossing (outside 165 iron mill lane) which is so over grown it’s forcing children into the road to walk and anything can happen in a split second. Thank you for taking the time to read this, I do hope we won’t be playing hop scotch with poop and glass much longer :-)
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Maiden Lane, Barnes Cray, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
